column1: # CANDIDATE screen, 2026-09-21 (OPUS): contract-named MUTABLE STATE with no declared type.
# Produced by applying the accepted types-MET criterion (SWE2-AUDIT-SEM, 8f7050694 - a cell cannot
# reach MET while a contract-named piece of state sits outside the store) to all 51 systems, so that
# the remaining PARTIAL cells carry enumerable work lists instead of an unexplained label.
# THIS IS A SUPERSET SCREEN, NOT A REQUIRED-WORK LIST, and the difference is load-bearing. The ruling
# scoped its two findings to state a contract names in its OWN sections (S-3 / S-5); this scans each
# contract document whole, so it also catches addresses cited in passing. Every row is a CANDIDATE
# for the auditor to accept or reject; none is a claim that the system owns that state.
# Filters, and why each exists: only .data (which carries BSS in its virtual tail) - .rdata is vtables,
# strings, RTTI and import thunks, and leaving it in inflated a first pass from 398 to 572; .text is
# excluded because a function is not state; addresses that are round multiples of 0x10000 are dropped
# as masks and bounds that merely parse as addresses. An address is DECLARED if types.tsv names it in
# route/instance/allocation_site, OR if it falls inside a declared type's extent - a field of an
# already-declared record is covered, and counting it would invent work the store has done.
# OVERLAP WITH AN EXISTING CHECK, stated rather than discovered later. check_contract_globals.py
# already enumerates the data globals contracts cite - it reports 684 where this finds 673, the
# difference being its .rdata rows and this one's round-number filter - and it classifies them by
# whether a WRITER is visible in the image. That is a different axis from this one, which asks
# whether the address is DECLARED IN _types. A global can have three visible writers and still be
# undeclared, and that is exactly the population the types-MET criterion is about. Anyone
# extending this should consider folding the declared/undeclared column into that checker rather
# than keeping two enumerations of the same citation set.
# HOW MUCH OF THE REMAINDER IS ACTUALLY DECLARABLE - measured, not assumed (OPUS, 2026-09-21).
# The rows left are NOT a list of that many declarations waiting to be written, and the densest
# system shows why. S-05's addresses cluster: 022D91A0..022D9330 holds eleven of them inside 0x190
# bytes. Two readings were possible - one record with eleven fields, or eleven separate statics -
# and the discriminator is whether code LEAs a base and indexes it or addresses each absolutely.
# Measured over that region: 8,806 direct rip-relative accesses at 104 DISTINCT addresses, against
# only 6 leas and ZERO accesses through an index register. So it is a dense block of individual
# globals - roughly one every four bytes - and neither response is right: declaring it as one
# record would invent a layout, and declaring 104 scalar types would bloat the store to describe a
# compiler's data segment. A block like this needs the auditor to scope WHICH of its addresses the
# contract actually leans on, which is a judgement, not a sweep.
# The rows that ARE straightforwardly declarable look like the thirteen already done on 2026-09-21:
# an isolated address with a small, complete reference set, where the instructions give a width, a
# direction and often the role outright. 01F44830 is the counter-example in the other direction - a
# single address with 2,216 references that turned out to be __security_cookie, cited by four
# contracts and owned by none of them.
#             base pointer, or data a page simply quotes. A row like this is NOT undeclared state;
# S-43 AND S-48'S LARGEST SHARED REGION, characterised 2026-09-21 (OPUS) so it is not swept.
# 02B40E00..02B41000 carries S-43's densest cluster (16 addresses) and sits beside S-48's
# 02B40518 cluster. The store describes NONE of it, so it is genuinely undeclared - but it is not
# one record. Measured: 214 direct rip-relative references at 18 distinct addresses, 15 leas at 7,
# and (see the WITHDRAWN clause below) across 24 functions concentrated in 003BA7B0/003BA990/003BAC90/
# 003BAEB0 - the resource-request layer the pages attribute it to. That is the same shape as
# S-05's block: module-level globals addressed absolutely, plus a few buffers whose addresses are
# taken (02B40EC8 receives a name copy). Declaring one record would invent a layout; declaring 18
# scalars would describe a translation unit's data segment.
# NOTE FOR WHOEVER SCOPES IT: the pages call 02B40E14 'a 402-byte state machine bounded at 0xF
# into a sixteen-arm jump table'. The 402 bytes are the FUNCTION's size, not the data's - the
# bracket in [02B40E14] means the cell holds the state value. The eight consecutive dwords at
# 02B40E00..02B40E28 are the plausible context record if a boundary is ever wanted, but nothing
# measured here establishes one.
# THE LARGEST UNDECLARED STRUCTURE IN THIS SCREEN, measured 2026-09-21 (OPUS): the band at
# 02EBF000..02EBF3FE, which S-09 names as the authored-data table registry and which S-04, S-14
# and S-32 also cite. It has 2,343 direct rip-relative references at 91 distinct addresses across
# 472 FUNCTIONS, 67 leas at 51 addresses, and ZERO indexed accesses; the gap between consecutive
# referenced addresses is 8 bytes in 73 of 90 cases. That is a slot table, and _types carries NO
# TYPE FOR IT - by reference count it is the single biggest gap the criterion has surfaced.
# IT IS NOT DECLARED HERE ON PURPOSE. FABLE has already read this band closely: their pages record
# a census over 02EBF000-02EBF178 across 239 functions, and answer 2026-09-12 that there is NO
# HEADER, that 02EBF000 is a float written by 0039AF20, and that 02EBF004 is unreferenced. A naive
# 'array of 8-byte slots from 02EBF000' would contradict all three of those findings on its first
# row. The declaration needs those readings reconciled with the slot spacing first, which is a
# semantic question for the band's owner and not something to settle from spacing alone.
# WITHDRAWN 2026-09-21 (OPUS): every 'ZERO indexed accesses' clause above. The test behind it
# asked whether the RIP-RELATIVE operand carried an index register, and an indexed table is not
# written that way. It is written `lea rcx,[table]` and then `[rax + rcx]`, with the index added
# AFTER the lea - 0032F6E3 and 003321B6 do exactly that on 022C6D20, which the pages describe as
# 022C6D20[m], a per-slot byte array. So that counter can never be non-zero for the pattern it was
# meant to rule out, and its zero was never evidence. The clause is withdrawn from all three
# region notes. What still stands in each is the independent evidence: the distinct-address count,
# the gap distribution, the store-and-pages check, and in S-05's case 8,806 references at 104
# addresses in 416 bytes. The conclusions are unchanged; one of their supports was not a support.
# THE RIGHT TEST, for whoever needs it: track the lea's destination register and look for an index
# on a memory operand based on THAT register - which is what SEED=slots in
# census_receiver_fixpoint.py already does, and another reason to use the kit's census rather than
# a fresh discriminator.
# AND THE QUESTION THE WITHDRAWN CLAUSE WAS SUPPOSED TO ANSWER, now answered with a test that
# passes its control (OPUS, 2026-09-21). The test: take the destination register of
# `lea reg,[table]` and look for a memory operand INDEXED off that register in the same body.
# CONTROL FIRST - 022C6D20, which the pages call 022C6D20[m] and whose two sites were read by
# hand: the test returns exactly those two, 0032F6EA `movsx eax, byte ptr [rax + rcx]` and
# 003321BD `mov byte ptr [rbx + rdx], 1`. Note SEED=slots does NOT cover this case and returns
# zero functions on that same known positive: that seed needs the indexed load to yield a
# POINTER it can follow, and this table holds bytes. Recommending it was my error.
#   S-05  022D91A0 : 0 indexed sites, 6 plain leas   -> separate globals, CONFIRMED.
#   S-43/48 02B40E00: 1 indexed site, at 02B40EC8 with a 16-byte movups - the name buffer being
#                     block-copied, not an element access -> module data block, CONFIRMED.
#   S-09  02EBF000 : 16 INDEXED SITES - the band really does contain indexed tables, and the
#                     strides are visible: 02EBF1A0 indexed by rax*8 and rcx*8 (qword elements,
#                     e.g. 00233E14 `cmp qword ptr [rcx + rax*8], 0`) and 02EBF278 by rsi*4
#                     (dword elements, 0022FFBF `movss dword ptr [rcx + rsi*4], xmm1`). That is
#                     concrete input for the slot-origin question routed to FABLE - the band is
#                     not one uniform table, it has at least two element widths at two bases.
# CONTROL, and it is the reason to trust the screen at all: S-01 and S-46 are the two systems the
# ruling scored by hand. After ten scalar declarations on 2026-09-21 this screen shows S-01 at ZERO
# remaining candidates and S-46 at one, and the addresses it had listed for them are exactly the
# ones the ruling named plus the wider-scan extras. The screen agrees with the hand scoring where
# they overlap. S-01 reaching zero here is NOT a MET verdict - re-scoring is the auditor's.
# WHAT THE REMAINING COUNT IS, measured 2026-09-21 (OPUS) and corrected twice on the way.
# Of the 338 distinct addresses the screen listed before this correction:
#    48  were ALREADY DESCRIBED in the store - just not in a cell this screen used to read. That
#        was a defect in the screen, not a gap in the store, and it is fixed: the declared-test now
#        reads fields.tsv and types.tsv whole. 02099FF0 is the case that exposed it - documented as
#        ActorManagerSlot's groupPersistentBank, 0x200 bytes over 77 offsets, in a field row's
#        evidence. After the fix the screen reports 314 rather than 368.
#    47  have NO CODE REFERENCE ANYWHERE. Nothing names them by absolute address: table entries
#        reached by index, interior fields off a base pointer, or data a page quotes.
#    53  are referenced ONLY by lea - record or array BASES, so ONE record declaration covers each.
#   205  are accessed by code AND described nowhere in the store. THAT is the honest remaining
#        declaration work - 61% of the raw count, and still an upper bound, because some of it is
#        machinery no subsystem owns (01F44830 is __security_cookie: 2,216 reads, four contracts
#        cite it, none owns it).
# A CAUTION FOR WHOEVER WORKS THE 53 BASES. Profiling them with an ad-hoc register tracker produced
# NEGATIVE displacements on four unrelated bases with the identical -0x80..+0x80 signature. Four
# unrelated types do not share one layout: the tracker was missing `lea rax,[rax+0x80]`, the pointer
# advance in an unrolled copy loop, so real offsets +0x00..+0x70 were recorded as negatives off the
# advanced pointer. census_receiver_fixpoint.py already handles that - it is one of the four fixes
# in its own docstring. USE IT rather than rebuilding a tracker without its fixes.
